_design_notes: Only PLAIN TERMS live here — the layer where drift was proven (e.g. 生态/破圈/蓝图 were in wechat's vocab but missing from X's, so the same sentence passed X and failed wechat). Regex constructions (首先…其次, not-just-X-but-Y) and frequency-capped craft words (novel's 不禁/仿佛 per-3000-char caps) stay in their own engines — merging them would erase legitimate per-genre differences.

This file carries ONLY {category -> terms}. It deliberately does NOT carry severity or treatment. Each engine decides how to treat a hit (X: warn; wechat: weighted score; novel: hard exit1). Same term, different genre, different consequence — that is correct, not drift.

`surfaces` is informational: which categories are RELEVANT to each skill. Engines reference `categories[<name>]` directly and map each category to its own rule/dimension (e.g. bait -> error, vocab -> warn). Do NOT flatten a surface's categories into one list.
